name: aida_r5_lab_vial_open
purpose: the user's task (2026-10-17), its first step: the capped pill vial opened. The vial clamped on the bench, the R5's left hand grips the cap in a tripod and turns it off its one-turn thread in strokes - turning, letting go, turning back, gripping again - then lifts it away (behaviors.cap_thread: the closure's hold, the thread's drag, the cap let go at the thread's end)

objects.name: Vial
objects.label: the capped pill vial
objects.why: the 30-dram vial, capped, its cap seated on its one-turn thread (make_pill_kit.cap_thread_pair)

clamp.why: held in a bench clamp while its cap is turned, as a holder or the other hand holds it (the R5's right hand is not yet in these takes)

grasp_plan.why: a tripod across the cap's skirt (thumb against index and middle), turned about the vial's axis 80 deg a stroke - the wrist's roll is +-55 to +-100 deg - the whole thread and 20 deg past it, then the cap lifted 4 cm

grasp_replay.why: the planned cap turn (plan_er_grasp.py, task cap_turn)
grasp_replay.controller_why: HomeHero's recordings and planner paths are commands to its R5 action layer (gravity-compensated arm targets, gravity feed-forward elsewhere); plain targets leave the shoulder slide 7.5 mm under its target (7.6 kg on 10 kN/m)

hand_model.why: the halt (word 007) set above the force band, 8.0 V, so the position loop governs the squeeze: at the 3.0 V default the index stalls at about 3 N, the band's floor, and could tighten no further. Driven by the grip command alone this pinch failed every way: at 3.0 V the thumb flicked the 14 g pawn out before it stalled; at 1.0 V with 0.8 V post-contact the digits crept closed during the carry and rolled it out at 61 deg; at 1.0 V with 0 V the stored 2.4 N drained in half a second of lift

grip.why: a twisting grip: the closure's hold of 0.15 N m at the cap's 22 mm radius is 6.8 N round its rim; the strokes broke it loose with the digits at 3-4 N. The floor at 2 N: in a tripod the thumb opposes index and middle at an angle and reads below them (2.5-2.9 N against 3.2-4.1) - with a 3 N floor the band never read 'loaded' and the lift that takes the freed cap away aborted (2026-10-18); under the fingertip's ~8 N stall

cap.why: the cap as tight as the R5's hand closes it (reasoned until a closing take measures it: three digits at ~5 N, friction ~0.9, on a 22 mm radius - 0.3 N m); a machine-capped 38 mm closure is applied at 1.9-2.9 N m (Oberk), past what the hand can turn
